Consult Summary:
- Adult with known asthma presented via telehealth with 2–3 days of exertional shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough with minimal relief from salbutamol; advised temporary increase of inhaled steroid dose, PRN reliever use, urgent GP review, and A&E if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath with wheeze and cough for 2–3 days.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset 2–3 days ago during a run; now also occurs with brisk walking.
  - Previously well-controlled asthma; last notable attack 3–4 years ago.
  - Current symptoms persist despite salbutamol; no sputum.
  - Has not checked peak flow since onset.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Exacerbated by exertion (running, brisk walking).
  - Limited relief with blue inhaler (salbutamol).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Wheeze, cough.
  - Denies sputum production.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No recent hospital admissions for asthma.
  - No prior use of oral steroids reported.
- Systems review: Limited to respiratory and allergic history as above.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Background: Longstanding; previously well controlled.
  - Last asthma attack: ~3–4 years ago.
  - No prior hospital admissions; no prior oral steroids recalled.
  - Last asthma review: ~2 years ago.
  - Baseline peak flow when well: approximately 380 (value approximated during consult).
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever).
- Possible eczema (patient reports skin issues that “could be eczema”; not formally diagnosed).

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (blue): PRN; currently used daily and sometimes morning/evening “to prevent”; dose/route/frequency not fully documented.
- Clenil (brown inhaler; beclomethasone): used twice daily; dose not documented. Advised to increase to 4 puffs twice daily temporarily.
- Cetraben: dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone: dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies. Environmental: hay fever.

Social History:
- Physically active; runs regularly.
- Tobacco use: not documented.
- Alcohol use: not documented.
- Other substances: not documented.
- Living situation/occupation/financial factors: not documented.

Family History:
- Brother: asthma.
- Sister: eczema.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telehealth). No vitals documented.

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.
- Planned at GP review: chest examination and peak flow measurement.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected mild asthma exacerbation over 2–3 days.
  - Plan:
    - Increase Clenil (brown inhaler) to 4 puffs twice daily while awaiting review.
    - Use salbutamol (blue inhaler) PRN up to every 2–4 hours; frequent need indicates poor control.
    - Book face-to-face GP appointment in the next few days for chest exam and peak flow assessment.
    - Safety net: If breathing worsens or if needing reliever very frequently, attend A&E and do not wait for scheduled appointment.
    - Depending on in-person findings, may require antibiotics and/or oral steroids (to be determined at review).
- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever).
  - Plan: No specific changes discussed during this consult.
- Issue 3: Possible eczema (not confirmed).
  - Plan: Currently using Cetraben and hydrocortisone; no changes discussed.

General Plan items:
- Reinforce follow-up: book face-to-face appointment within a few days.
- Continue current medications as above with temporary inhaled steroid up-titration.
- Consider checking inhaler technique and providing an asthma action plan at in-person review (not performed today).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals (including O2 saturation), physical exam, current peak flow during symptoms.
  - Full medication reconciliation with doses/routes/frequencies.
  - Smoking status, alcohol/substance use, occupation, triggers, recent infections, vaccine status.
  - Inhaler technique and spacer use not assessed.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Preventer identification initially unclear (patient said “blue” when asked about preventer; later aligned with doctor’s reference to brown Clenil).
  - Medication list initially included unclear terms (“Flanel Bactroban”); later corrected to Cetraben and hydrocortisone.
  - Reliever frequency guidance stated as “every 2–4 hours,” later “up to every 2 hourly” (minor variation).
  - Baseline peak flow “about 380” was suggested by clinician and agreed by patient; approximate.
- Transcript quality:
  - Several unclear/inaudible segments and overlaps; some medication names difficult to verify; dose specifics not obtained.
